question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'. You are so far the bright student in the class.
explanation: Comparing one student with the whole class needs the superlative, and "by far" is the idiom used to stress it: "by far the brightest". Answer: by far the brightest

subject: English Comprehension
question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Vivek should be excited / on the promotion / he’s got.
explanation: "Excited" takes "about" (or "at"), not "on": "excited about the promotion". The error is in "on the promotion". Answer: on the promotion

subject: English Comprehension
question: The following sentence has been split into segments. One of them may contain an error. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Among you and me / she is quite rude / to the boy.
explanation: "Between" is used for two people (you and me); "among" is for more than two. The error is "Among you and me". Answer: Among you and me

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. She is looking after the old ladies with great affection.

options.A: The old ladies are being looked after with great affection.
options.B: The old ladies are looked after with great affection.
options.C: She is looked after with great affection by the old ladies.
options.D: The old ladies were looked after with great affection.

explanation: Present continuous active (is looking after) becomes "are being looked after" in the passive, with the plural subject "the old ladies". Answer: The old ladies are being looked after with great affection.

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Tall promises were being made by each promoter.

options.A: Each promoter has made tall promises.
options.B: Each promoter was making tall promises.
options.C: Each promoter has been making tall promises.

explanation: "Were being made" is past continuous passive, so the active form is past continuous: "Each promoter was making tall promises." Answer: Each promoter was making tall promises.

question: Which of the following is NOT a broad mitigation technique of landslide?

options.D: Construction of retention wall to stop land from slipping

explanation: Landslide mitigation includes hazard mapping, surface drainage control and retaining walls. Vegetation binds the soil, so reducing it makes landslides more likely; it is not a mitigation measure. Answer: Reduction in the vegetation cover to arrest landslide

question: Colloidal systems – such as gum, starch, proteins, cellulose, agar and gelatine – when placed in water, will absorb a large volume of water and swell up. These substances are called ______.
explanation: Hydrophilic colloids such as gum, starch, proteins, cellulose, agar and gelatine absorb water and swell; this is imbibition, and such substances are called imbibants. Answer: imbibants

question: As per World Justice Project 2020, what is India’s rank in Regulatory Enforcement as cited in Economic Survey of India 2021?
explanation: The Economic Survey 2020-21 cites the World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2020, in which India ranks 74th on the Regulatory Enforcement factor. Answer: 74

question: ______, the world’s first sailing boat made entirely from plastic waste, aims to raise people’s awareness of plastic pollution in oceans.

explanation: Wavelength is the horizontal distance between two successive crests (or troughs). Wave height is vertical; wave period is a time. Answer: Wave length

question: The 61st Amendment to the Constitution of India ______.

options.A: exempted Arunachal Pradesh from reservation for Scheduled Castes in Panchayati Raj institutions
options.B: reduced the age for voting from 21 to 18 years
options.D: restricted the size of council of ministers to 15% of the number of legislative members

explanation: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years (Article 326). Answer: reduced the age for voting from 21 to 18 years

explanation: The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in 1955. Answer: 1955

subject: General Awareness
question: If cosec A = sec B, where A and B are acute angles, then what is the value of (A + B)?
explanation: cosec A = sec(90° − A), so sec(90° − A) = sec B. For acute angles this gives B = 90° − A, i.e. A + B = 90°. Answer: 90°

subject: General Awareness
question: A solid cone of radius 7 cm and height 7 cm was melted along with two solid spheres of radius 7 cm each to form a solid cylinder of radius 7 cm. What is the curved surface area (in cm 2 ) of the cylinder? (Use π = 22/7)
explanation: Total volume = (1/3)π(7²)(7) + 2 × (4/3)π(7³) = π × 7³ × (1/3 + 8/3) = 3 × 343π = 1029π. Cylinder: π × 7² × h = 1029π, so h = 21 cm. Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 21 = 924 cm². Answer: 924

subject: General Awareness
question: A tyre has two punctures. The first puncture alone would have made the tyre flat in 45 minutes, and the second puncture alone would have done it in 90 minutes. If air leaks out at a constant rate, then how long (in minutes) does it take for both the punctures together to make the tyre flat?
explanation: Per minute the two punctures let out 1/45 + 1/90 = 3/90 = 1/30 of the air. So together they take 30 minutes. Answer: 30

subject: General Awareness
question: A and B entered into a partnership with investments in the ratio 3 : 5. After a few months, A withdrew and collected back his money. At the end of the year, they received profit in the ratio 2 : 5. After how many months did A withdraw?
explanation: If A stayed t months: (3 × t) : (5 × 12) = 2 : 5. 15t = 120, so t = 8 months. Answer: 8

subject: General Awareness
question: If (sin 2 θ − 3sinθ + 2)/cos 2 θ = 1, where 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of (cos2θ − sin3θ + cosec2θ)?
explanation: sin²θ − 3sinθ + 2 = cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ gives 2sin²θ − 3sinθ + 1 = 0, so sinθ = 1/2 or 1. As θ < 90°, θ = 30°. cos60° − sin90° + cosec60° = 1/2 − 1 + 2/√3 = −1/2 + 2√3/3 = (−3 + 4√3)/6. Answer: (−3 + 4√3)/6

subject: General Awareness
question: In the month of March, Dalip earned on an average ₹501 per day. For the first 18 days, his average earning was ₹495 and, for the last 15 days, his average earning was ₹505. On 18 th March, he earned ₹50 more than that earned on 17 th March. How much (in ₹) did he earn on 18 th March?
explanation: March total = 31 × 501 = ₹15,531. First 18 days = 18 × 495 = ₹8,910; last 15 days (17th–31st) = 15 × 505 = ₹7,575. The 17th and 18th are counted twice: 8,910 + 7,575 − 15,531 = ₹954. If the 17th earned x, then x + (x + 50) = 954, so x = 452 and the 18th = ₹502. Answer: 502

subject: General Awareness
question: In ΔABC, the perpendiculars drawn from A, B and C meet the opposite sides at points D, E and F, respectively. AD, BE and CF intersect at point P. If ∠EPD = 110° and the bisectors of ∠A and ∠B meet at point Q, then ∠AQB = ?
explanation: P is the orthocentre; in quadrilateral CDPE the angles at D and E are 90°, so ∠C = 180° − ∠EPD = 70°. Q is the incentre, so ∠AQB = 90° + ∠C/2 = 90° + 35° = 125°. Answer: 125°

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. GTQ : JVP :: SDK : ?
explanation: G + 3 = J, T + 2 = V and Q − 1 = P. Apply the same shifts to SDK: S + 3 = V, D + 2 = F, K − 1 = J, giving VFJ. Answer: VFJ

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. CLAY, DIFX, EFKW, FCPV, ?
explanation: Read each position separately: first letters C, D, E, F → G (+1); second letters L, I, F, C → Z (−3, wrapping round); third letters A, F, K, P → U (+5); fourth letters Y, X, W, V → U (−1). So the next cluster is GZUU. Answer: GZUU

question: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
explanation: In CEV, QSH and KMN the second letter is two places after the first (C→E, Q→S, K→M). In MPI the gap is three (M→P), so MPI is the odd one. Answer: MPI

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Introducing Reshma to a guest, a lady, Karishma, said, “She is the daughter of my father-in-law’s daughter”. How is Reshma related to Karishma?
explanation: Karishma's father-in-law's daughter is her husband's sister. Reshma is the daughter of her husband's sister, i.e. Karishma's niece. Answer: Niece

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 13+15×8 ÷96−4=109
explanation: Interchange ÷ and −: 13 + 15 × 8 − 96 ÷ 4. = 13 + 120 − 24 = 109, which matches the right-hand side. Answer: ÷ and −

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: In a certain code language, 'BLUES' is written as 'HVFOY'. How will 'FORCED' be written in that language?
explanation: Write BLUES backwards (SEULB) and replace each letter by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, …): S→H, E→V, U→F, L→O, B→Y, giving HVFOY. FORCED backwards is DECROF; opposites: D→W, E→V, C→X, R→I, O→L, F→U, giving WVXILU. Answer: WVXILU

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Malice 2. Malignant 3. Mallows 4. Malfunction 5. Malware
explanation: All words begin with "Mal"; compare the following letters: Malf-, Malic-, Malig-, Mall-, Malw-. Order: Malfunction, Malice, Malignant, Mallows, Malware = 4, 1, 2, 3, 5. Answer: 4, 1, 2, 3, 5

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 74, 101, 128, 155, ?
explanation: Each term is 27 more than the previous one: 74, 101, 128, 155. 155 + 27 = 182. Answer: 182

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some spades are knives. All knives are rakes. Conclusions: I. Some knives are spades. II. Some rakes are knives.

options.B: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
options.C: Both conclusions I and II follow.

explanation: "Some spades are knives" converts to "Some knives are spades", so I follows. "All knives are rakes" means every knife is a rake, so "Some rakes are knives" is true; II follows. Answer: Both conclusions I and II follow.

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: In a certain code language, ‘MOHAN’ is coded as 39-45-24-3-42 and ‘KABIR’ is coded as 33-3-6-27-54. How will ‘RAGHU’ be coded in that language?
explanation: Each letter is replaced by three times its position in the alphabet: M = 13 × 3 = 39, O = 15 × 3 = 45, H = 24, A = 3, N = 42. RAGHU: R = 54, A = 3, G = 21, H = 24, U = 63. Answer: 54-3-21-24-63

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Four friends, H, I, J and K, are sitting at the four corners of a square facing towards the centre. H and J are sitting at diagonally opposite corners. I is sitting to the immediate left of H. Who is sitting to the immediate right of J?
explanation: When people face the centre, a person’s immediate left is the next seat clockwise. Going clockwise: H, I, J, K (H and J are diagonal). J’s immediate right is the previous seat clockwise, which is I. Answer: I

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 14, 20, 34, 72, 182, ?
explanation: Differences: 6, 14, 38, 110. Each difference is 3 × previous − 4 (6 × 3 − 4 = 14, 14 × 3 − 4 = 38, 38 × 3 − 4 = 110). Next difference = 110 × 3 − 4 = 326, so the term is 182 + 326 = 508. Answer: 508

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: In a certain code, ‘Tim Dim Kim’ means ‘India Is Big’ and ‘Dim Gim Kim Se Rim’ means ‘Tiger Is A Big Cat’. Which of the following is the code for ‘India’?
explanation: "Dim" and "Kim" appear in both coded sentences, as do "Is" and "Big". The remaining code in the first sentence, "Tim", therefore means "India". Answer: Tim

question: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. IMM_ _ILEI_ _OBI_ _IMMO_ _LE
explanation: The series is the word IMMOBILE written three times: IMMOBILE IMMOBILE IMMOBILE. The blanks are filled by O, B, M, M, L, E, B, I = OBMMLEBI. Answer: OBMMLEBI

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in it. 12 36 60 72 3 4 63 4 12 98 ? 15 12 9 14
explanation: In each figure, centre = (left ÷ bottom) − (top ÷ right). Figure 1: 72 ÷ 12 − 12 ÷ 4 = 6 − 3 = 3. Figure 2: 63 ÷ 9 − 36 ÷ 12 = 7 − 3 = 4. Figure 3: 98 ÷ 14 − 60 ÷ 15 = 7 − 4 = 3. Answer: 3

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Which of the following British officers issued the infamous ‘crawling order’ whereby Indians had to crawl on all fours to pass an alley?
explanation: After the assault on missionary Marcella Sherwood in Amritsar (April 1919), Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer issued the "crawling order", forcing Indians to crawl along the street where she was attacked. Answer: General Dyer

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: The ancient city of Champa is believed to be the capital of ______ Mahajanapada.
explanation: Champa, near present-day Bhagalpur in Bihar, was the capital of the Anga mahajanapada. Answer: Anga

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Gulzar was awarded the 66th Filmfare Award for ‘Best Lyrics’ for the film ______.
explanation: At the 66th Filmfare Awards (2021), Gulzar won Best Lyrics for the title song of "Chhapaak". Answer: Chhapaak

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Which of the following is NOT a type of mosquito?
explanation: Culex, Anopheles and Aedes are mosquito genera. Limulus is the horseshoe crab, an arthropod related to spiders and scorpions. Answer: Limulus

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Which of the following is the middle layer in the root apical meristem that gives rise to the cortex?
explanation: In the root apex (histogen theory), dermatogen forms the epidermis, periblem (the middle layer) forms the cortex, and plerome forms the stele; calyptrogen forms the root cap. Answer: Periblem

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Mridula Sinha, who passed away in November 2020, was the first woman Governor of ______.
explanation: Writer Mridula Sinha served as Governor of Goa from 2014 to 2019 and was its first woman Governor. She died in November 2020. Answer: Goa

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Normally, there is a ______ day interval between spring tides and neap tides.
explanation: Spring tides occur at new and full moon, neap tides at the quarter phases, so the two are about seven days apart. Answer: seven

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: A ladder 18 m long rests against a wall so that the angle between the ladder and the wall is 30°. How far (in m) is the base of the ladder from the wall?
explanation: The distance from the wall is opposite the 30° angle at the wall: 18 × sin30° = 18 × 1/2 = 9 m. Answer: 9

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: A person’s salary was increased by 50% and subsequently decreased by 50%. How much percentage does he lose or gain?
explanation: Net change = 50 − 50 − (50 × 50)/100 = −25%. So he loses 25% (e.g. 100 → 150 → 75). Answer: Loss of 25%

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: What is the sum of the numbers between 400 and 500 such that when they are divided by 6, 12 and 16, it leaves no remainder?
explanation: The numbers must be multiples of LCM(6, 12, 16) = 48. Between 400 and 500 these are 432 and 480; their sum is 912. Answer: 912

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: If a 2 + b 2 = 65 and ab = 8, a > b > 0, then find the value of a 2 − b 2 .

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: The given pie chart shows the percentage of students in five schools and the table shows the ratio of boys and girls in each school. Study the pie chart and table and answer the question that follows. (Data from the official pie chart, shown as a table.) School Percentage of students A 28% B 15% C 24% D 18% E 15% The below table shows the ratio of girls and boys in the given five schools. School Girls : Boys A 3 : 4 B 2 : 3 C 5 : 3 D 1 : 2 E 4 : 1 The number of girls in school D is what percentage less than the number of boys in school B (correct to the nearest integer)?
explanation: Take the total as 100 units. Girls in D = 18 × 1/3 = 6; boys in B = 15 × 3/5 = 9. (9 − 6)/9 × 100 = 33.3% ≈ 33%. Answer: 33%

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: If x 4 − 79x 2 + 1 = 0, then a value of x + x −1 can be:
explanation: Divide by x²: x² + 1/x² = 79. (x + 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² + 2 = 81, so x + 1/x = 9 (or −9). Answer: 9

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: If a nine-digit number 485x3678y is divisible by 72, then for the smallest value of x, the value of (2y − 3x) is:
explanation: Divisible by 8: the last three digits 78y must be divisible by 8, so y = 4 (784 = 8 × 98). Divisible by 9: the digit sum 4 + 8 + 5 + x + 3 + 6 + 7 + 8 + 4 = 45 + x must be a multiple of 9, so the smallest x is 0. 2y − 3x = 8 − 0 = 8. Answer: 8

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: The following bar graph shows the total number of youth (in lakhs) and the number of employed youth (in lakhs) in 5 states A, B, C, D and E. (Data from the official chart, shown as a table.) State Youth (lakhs) Employed youth (lakhs) A 12 10.5 B 8 7 C 11.5 10 D 10 7.5 E 9 8 How many youth (in lakhs) are unemployed in states B and D taken together?
explanation: Unemployed = youth − employed: B = 8 − 7 = 1 lakh; D = 10 − 7.5 = 2.5 lakh. Together = 3.5 lakh. Answer: 3.5

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: What is the compound interest (in ₹) on a sum of ₹62,500 for 2 years at 12% p.a., if the interest is compounded 8-monthly?
explanation: 8 months is 2/3 of a year: rate per period = 12 × 2/3 = 8%, and 2 years = 3 periods. Amount = 62,500 × 1.08³ = 62,500 × 1.259712 = ₹78,732; CI = 78,732 − 62,500 = ₹16,232. Answer: 16,232

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O. C and D are two points on the circle on either side of AB, such that ∠CAB = 52° and ∠ABD = 47°. What is the difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD?
explanation: Angles in a semicircle: ∠ACB = ∠ADB = 90°, so ∠CBA = 38° and ∠DAB = 43°. ∠CAD = 52° + 43° = 95° and ∠CBD = 38° + 47° = 85°; the difference is 10°. Answer: 10

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Study the graph and answer the question that follows. (Data from the official histogram, shown as a table.) Daily wages (in ₹) Number of workers 400–450 30 450–500 45 500–550 65 550–600 60 600–650 55 650–700 35 What is the ratio of the total number of workers whose daily wages are less than ₹450 to the total number of workers whose daily wages are ₹650 and above?
explanation: Wages below ₹450: 30 workers. Wages ₹650 and above: 35 workers. 30 : 35 = 6 : 7. Answer: 6 : 7

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: The breakup of the total number of employees of a company working in different offices (A to E), in degrees, is given in the pie chart. Total number of employees = 2400. (Data from the official pie chart, shown as a table.) Office Central angle A 126° B 18° C 54° D 90° E 72° If the percentage of male employees in office C is 20% and that of female employees in E is 40%, then what is the ratio of the numbers of female employees in E to that of female employees in C?
explanation: C = 54/360 × 2400 = 360 employees, of whom 80% = 288 are female. E = 72/360 × 2400 = 480 employees, of whom 40% = 192 are female. 192 : 288 = 2 : 3. Answer: 2 : 3

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: AB and CD are two chords in a circle with centre O and AD is the diameter. When produced, AB and CD meet at the point P. If ∠DAP = 27°, ∠APD = 35°, then what is the measure (in degrees) of ∠DBC?
explanation: AD is a diameter, so ∠ACD = 90°, and hence ∠ACP = 90° (P lies on line DC). In ΔACP, ∠CAP = 90° − 35° = 55°, so ∠DAC = 55° − 27° = 28°. ∠DBC and ∠DAC stand on the same arc DC, so ∠DBC = 28°. Answer: 28

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: A shopkeeper marks an article x % above the cost price and sells it by allowing 30% discount on the marked price. If there is a loss of 4.8%, then what is the value of x ?
explanation: With CP = 100, SP = 95.2, and SP = 0.7 × MP, so MP = 95.2/0.7 = 136. So the mark-up is x = 36%. Answer: 36

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Two trains are running on parallel tracks in the same direction at the speed of 80 km/h and 90 km/h, respectively. The trains crossed each other in 3 minutes. If the length of one train is 230 m, then what is the length (in m) of the other train?
explanation: Relative speed = 10 km/h = 10,000/60 m per minute, so in 3 minutes the faster train gains 500 m. Sum of lengths = 500 m, so the other train is 500 − 230 = 270 m. Answer: 270

subject: General Awareness
question: Which of the following Dynasties established the kingdom of Vijayanagara?
explanation: The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty. The Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties ruled later. Answer: Sangama Dynasty

subject: General Awareness
question: A ’Camel Protection and Development Policy’ has been announced by the government of _______.
explanation: Rajasthan, where the camel is the state animal, announced a Camel Protection and Development Policy (2022-23 budget) to check the falling camel population. Answer: Rajasthan

subject: General Awareness
question: What is the unit of work done?
explanation: Work = force × displacement, measured in joules (1 J = 1 N × 1 m). The decibel measures sound level, the ampere current and the watt power. Answer: Joule

subject: General Awareness
question: ______ part of xylem tissue in plants stores food.
explanation: Xylem parenchyma is the only living component of xylem; it stores food (starch) and helps in lateral conduction of water. Tracheids, vessels and xylem fibres are dead. Answer: Xylem parenchyma

subject: General Awareness
question: What theme was decided to celebrate the second ‘International Day of Yoga’ in India?

options.A: Yoga for the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals

explanation: The second International Day of Yoga (21 June 2016) was marked at the UN under the theme “Yoga for the Achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals”; it is the only matching option. Note: India’s own AYUSH theme for 2016 was “Connect the Youth”. Answer: Yoga for the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals

subject: General Awareness
question: The wearing away of the landscape by different agents such as water, wind and ice is called ______.
explanation: Erosion is the wearing away and removal of the land surface by agents such as running water, wind and ice (glaciers). Weathering breaks rocks in place, without transport. Answer: Erosion

subject: General Awareness
question: The chemical formula of quick lime is ______.
explanation: Quick lime is calcium oxide, CaO. Slaked lime is Ca(OH)₂ and limestone is CaCO₃. Answer: CaO

subject: General Awareness
question: Who among the following Presidents of India was also the deputy chairman of Planning Commission?
explanation: Pranab Mukherjee was Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission (1991–96) and later the 13th President of India (2012–17). Answer: Pranab Mukherjee

subject: General Awareness
question: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded a reform association named the Brahma Sabha, which later came to be known as ______.
explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahma Sabha in 1828; it later came to be known as the Brahmo Samaj. Answer: Brahmo Samaj

subject: General Awareness
question: When was ‘Vayudoot’ airline setup in India?
explanation: Vayudoot, a regional/feeder airline, was set up in 1981; it was merged into Indian Airlines in 1993. Answer: 1981

subject: General Awareness
question: Who among the following composers won the Grammy in 2015 for his album ‘Winds of Samsara’ – a collaboration with South African flautist Wouter Kellerman?
explanation: Bengaluru-based composer Ricky Kej won the 2015 Grammy for Best New Age Album for “Winds of Samsara”, made with South African flautist Wouter Kellerman. Answer: Ricky Kej

subject: General Awareness
question: Burning of coal is an example of ______.
explanation: Coal (carbon) burns in oxygen: C + O₂ → CO₂. Two reactants form a single product, so it is a combination reaction. Answer: combination reaction

subject: General Awareness
question: The Ramakrishna Mission stressed the ideal of __________ through social service and selfless work.
explanation: The Ramakrishna Mission (founded by Swami Vivekananda, 1897) stressed the ideal of salvation (moksha) through social service and selfless work. Answer: Moksha (salvation)

subject: General Awareness
question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated in Punjab to commemorate the formation of the Khalsa Panth?
explanation: Baisakhi (13/14 April) marks the founding of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh at Anandpur Sahib in 1699; it is also the harvest festival of Punjab. Answer: Baisakhi

subject: General Awareness
question: The word ‘Parliament’ refers to the _________.
explanation: Under Article 79, Parliament is the national legislature of India: the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. State legislatures are separate bodies. Answer: National legislature

subject: General Awareness
question: Who was appointed as the new Chairman of the Central Board of Direct Taxes in June 2022?
explanation: Nitin Gupta, a 1986-batch IRS officer, was appointed Chairman of the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) in June 2022. Answer: Nitin Gupta

subject: General Awareness
question: In Golgi apparatus, the maturing face is:
explanation: SSC’s key gives “convex”. However, the standard description (NCERT Class XI) is that Golgi cisternae have a convex cis or forming face and a concave trans or maturing face, which points to “concave”. Answer: convex

subject: General Awareness
question: The foremost right among the rights to freedom is the _______.

options.A: Right to life and personal liberty
options.C: Right to freedom of speech and expression

explanation: Among the freedom rights (Articles 19–22), the right to life and personal liberty (Article 21) is regarded as the most important and fundamental; even preventive detention is an exception to it. Answer: Right to life and personal liberty

subject: General Awareness
question: The mean proportion of 169 and 144 is:
explanation: Mean proportional of a and b = √(ab) = √(169 × 144) = 13 × 12 = 156. Answer: 156

subject: General Awareness
question: How many spherical lead shots each of diameter 8.4 cm can be obtained from a rectangular solid of lead with dimension 88 cm, 63 cm, 42 cm (take π = 22/7)?
explanation: Volume of the solid = 88 × 63 × 42 = 2,32,848 cm³. Radius of a shot = 4.2 cm, so its volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × 4.2³ = 310.464 cm³. Number of shots = 232848 ÷ 310.464 = 750. Answer: 750

subject: General Awareness
question: Riya could not decide between discount of 30% or two successive discounts of 25% and 5%, both given on shopping of ₹3,840. What is the difference between both the discounts?
explanation: Single discount: 30% of 3840 = ₹1,152. Successive 25% and 5%: net = 25 + 5 − (25 × 5)/100 = 28.75%, i.e. ₹1,104. Difference = 1152 − 1104 = ₹48. Answer: ₹48

subject: General Awareness
question: In the triangle ABC, AB = 12 cm and AC = 10 cm, and ∠BAC = 60°. What is the value of the length of the side BC?
explanation: By the cosine rule, BC² = AB² + AC² − 2·AB·AC·cos 60° = 144 + 100 − 2 × 12 × 10 × ½ = 124. BC = √124 ≈ 11.13 cm. Answer: 11.13 cm

subject: General Awareness
question: The table given below shows the number of spoon manufactured by five factories. Factory Spoon P 100 Q 200 R 150 S 50 T 250 What are the ratio of number of spoon manufactured by P to the number of spoon manufactured by R?
explanation: P manufactured 100 spoons and R 150, so P : R = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3. Answer: 2 : 3

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 21 * 4 * 156 * 13 * 11 = 83
explanation: Try option 1 (×, −, ÷, +): 21 × 4 − 156 ÷ 13 + 11 = 84 − 12 + 11 = 83. ✔ The other combinations do not give 83. Answer: ×, −, ÷, +

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 12 * 24 * 4 * 2 * 60
explanation: With +, ×, ÷, =: 12 + 24 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 + 48 = 60, which balances the equation. Option 1 gives a negative value, option 2 gives 24 and option 4 gives 106. Answer: +, ×, ÷, =

explanation: RQP, LKJ and HGF are three consecutive letters in reverse alphabetical order. UVW runs forward, so it is the odd one. Answer: UVW

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. NMRQ, NDZG, NUHW, NLPM, ?
explanation: The first letter is always N. Second letters go back 9 each time (M → D → U → L → C), third letters go forward 8 (R → Z → H → P → X) and fourth letters go back 10 (Q → G → W → M → C). Next term: NCXC. Answer: NCXC

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ A & B means ‘A is the husband of B’ A % B means ‘A is the father of B’ If A % B & C # D @ E, then how is B related to E?
explanation: A % B: A is B’s father. B & C: B is C’s husband. C # D: C is D’s sister. D @ E: D is E’s daughter, so C is also E’s daughter. B is the husband of E’s daughter, i.e. E’s son-in-law. Answer: Son-in-law

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: If A × B means that A is the brother of B, A – B means that A is the sister of B, A + B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the paternal aunt of R?
explanation: P – Q + R: P is the sister of Q, and Q is the father of R. So P is the sister of R’s father, i.e. R’s paternal aunt. Answer: P – Q + R

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: In a certain code language, FRUCTUS is coded as 108, and SPRINTER is coded as 119. How will MASCULINE be coded in that language?
explanation: The code is the sum of the alphabet positions: FRUCTUS = 6 + 18 + 21 + 3 + 20 + 21 + 19 = 108; SPRINTER = 19 + 16 + 18 + 9 + 14 + 20 + 5 + 18 = 119. MASCULINE = 13 + 1 + 19 + 3 + 21 + 12 + 9 + 14 + 5 = 97. Answer: 97

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Select the odd group of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
explanation: In each group the second number is the cube of the first and the third is 10 less: 216 − 10 = 206, 125 − 10 = 115, 64 − 10 = 54. For 7, 343 − 12 = 331, so (7 – 343 – 331) is the odd group. Answer: (7 – 343 – 331)

question: In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. III. No W is D.

options.C: Both conclusions I and III follows
options.D: Both conclusions I and II follows

explanation: All W are S, so some S are W: conclusion I follows. No D is W is the same as no W is D: conclusion III follows. Nothing says all S are D, so II does not follow. Answer: Both conclusions I and III follows

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (20, 6, 4) (24, 7, 5)
explanation: First number = (second)² − (third)²: 6² − 4² = 20 and 7² − 5² = 24. Check the options: 9² − 4² = 81 − 16 = 65, so (65, 9, 4) follows the rule. Answer: (65, 9, 4)

explanation: Second number = (first − 1)²: (19 − 1)² = 324 and (25 − 1)² = 576. (9 − 1)² = 64. Answer: 64

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: In a certain code language, ’BEHOLD’ is written as ’BDEHLO’ and ’INDEED’ is written as ’DDEEIN’. How will ’COURSE’ be written in that language?
explanation: The letters of each word are rewritten in alphabetical order: BEHOLD → BDEHLO, INDEED → DDEEIN. COURSE → C, E, O, R, S, U = CEORSU. Answer: CEORSU

options.C: Only conclusions II and III follow

explanation: Cards ⊂ boxes ⊂ torches ⊂ shoes, so all cards are shoes: IV follows. I, II and III reverse an “All” statement, which is not allowed. Answer: Only conclusion IV follows

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Which of the following numbers is a divisor of (49 15 − 1)?
explanation: xⁿ − 1 is always divisible by x − 1. So 49¹⁵ − 1 is divisible by 49 − 1 = 48, and hence by every factor of 48. Of the options only 8 divides 48 (14, 46 and 50 are not guaranteed; 50 divides 49ⁿ + 1 for odd n, not 49ⁿ − 1). Answer: 8

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: In a 1500 m race, Anil beats Bakul by 150 m and in the same race Bakul beats Charles by 75 m. By what distance does Anil beat Charles?
explanation: When Anil runs 1500 m, Bakul runs 1350 m. Bakul beats Charles by 75 m in 1500 m, so when Bakul runs 1350 m Charles runs 1350 × 1425/1500 = 1282.5 m. Anil beats Charles by 1500 − 1282.5 = 217.50 m. Answer: 217.50 m

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: P and Q can complete a project in 15 days and 10 days, respectively. They started doing the work together, but after 2 days, Q had to leave and P alone completed the remaining work. In how many days was the whole work completed?
explanation: Together P and Q do 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6 per day; in 2 days they finish 1/3. P finishes the remaining 2/3 in (2/3) × 15 = 10 days. Total time = 2 + 10 = 12 days. Answer: 12

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Two circles touch each other externally at P. AB is a direct common tangent to the two circles, A and B are points of contact, and ∠PAB = 40° . The measure of ∠ABP is:
explanation: For two circles touching externally, the direct common tangent subtends a right angle at the point of contact: ∠APB = 90°. So ∠ABP = 180° − 90° − 40° = 50°. Answer: 50°

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: The following table shows the number of pages printed by 3 printers during 3 days. Days / Printers X Y Z Monday 130 140 210 Tuesday 110 145 160 Wednesday 180 90 218 What is the average number of pages printed by printer Z during the 3 days?
explanation: Pages printed by Z = 210 + 160 + 218 = 588. Average = 588 ÷ 3 = 196. Answer: 196

question: The length and breadth of a rectangle are increased by 8% and 5%, respectively. By how much percentage will the area of the rectangle increase?
explanation: Net change in area = 8 + 5 + (8 × 5)/100 = 13.4%. Answer: 13.4%

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: A dishonest merchant sells goods at a 12.5% loss on the cost price, but uses 28 g weight instead of 36 g. What is his percentage profit or loss?
explanation: Take the cost price as ₹1 per gram. For goods actually worth 28 g he charges the selling price of 36 g at a 12.5% loss: 36 × 0.875 = ₹31.5. Gain = (31.5 − 28)/28 × 100 = 12.5%. Answer: 12.5% gain

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: The HCF of two numbers is 12. Which one of the following can never be their LCM?
explanation: The LCM is always a multiple of the HCF. 72, 84 and 60 are multiples of 12, but 90 is not, so 90 can never be the LCM. Answer: 90

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: In a right-angled triangle PQR, right-angled at Q, the length of the side PR is 17 units, length of the base QR is 8 units, and length of the side PQ is 15 units. If ∠RPQ = α, then sinα + cosα is:
explanation: For angle α at P, the opposite side is QR = 8 and the adjacent side is PQ = 15, with hypotenuse PR = 17. sin α + cos α = 8/17 + 15/17 = 23/17. Answer: 23/17

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Radius of a circle is 10 cm. Angle made by chord AB at the centre of this circle is 60 degree. What is the length of this chord?
explanation: OA = OB = 10 cm and ∠AOB = 60°, so triangle AOB is equilateral. Hence AB = 10 cm. Answer: 10 cm

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: The batting average for 27 innings of a cricket player is 47 runs. His highest score in an innings exceeds his lowest score by 157 runs. If these two innings are excluded, the average score of the remaining 25 innings is 42 runs. Find his highest score in an innings.
explanation: Total of 27 innings = 27 × 47 = 1269; total of the other 25 = 25 × 42 = 1050. So highest + lowest = 219 and highest − lowest = 157. Highest = (219 + 157)/2 = 188. Answer: 188

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: The pie chart given below shows the number of truck sold by 8 different companies. The total number of truck sold by all these 8 companies are 4000. Number of truck sold by a particular company is shown as a percent of total number of truck sold by all these 8 companies. (Data from the official chart, shown as a table.) Company Percentage of trucks sold A 13% B 27% C 18% D 12% E 3% F 7% G 6% H 14% The number of trucks sold by B, C, F and H is how much percent less than the number of trucks sold by all these 8 companies?
explanation: B + C + F + H = 27% + 18% + 7% + 14% = 66% of the total. So these four sold 100 − 66 = 34 percent less than all eight companies together. Answer: 34 percent

options.B: Both conclusions I and II follows
options.D: Both conclusions I and III follows

explanation: All B are inside Q and no P is in Q, so no P is B: I follows. Since no Q is P, the Qs that exist are not P, so “Some Q are not P” follows. III contradicts “All B are Q”, so it does not follow. Answer: Both conclusions I and II follows

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: In a certain code language, 'ABASE’ is coded as 'ZEZVD' and 'BANDS' is coded as 'EZQGV'. How will 'CABIN' be coded in that language?
explanation: Vowels move one step back and consonants three steps forward: ABASE → A−1 = Z, B+3 = E, A−1 = Z, S+3 = V, E−1 = D; BANDS → E Z Q G V. CABIN → C+3 = F, A−1 = Z, B+3 = E, I−1 = H, N+3 = Q = FZEHQ. Answer: FZEHQ

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Cells : Tissue :: Organs : ?
explanation: Cells group together to form a tissue; organs group together to form the body (through organ systems). Answer: Body

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: In ‘Andes Mountain’ of South America animal which is used for transportation is ______.
explanation: The llama is the traditional pack animal of the Andes; it is sure-footed at high altitudes where camels and bullocks cannot work. Answer: Llamas

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Which Indian musician served as the artistic director of the World Music Department at the Rotterdam Music Conservatory in the Netherlands?
explanation: Flute maestro Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia served as artistic director of the World Music Department at the Rotterdam Music Conservatory (Codarts) in the Netherlands. Answer: Hariprasad Chaurasia

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Which of the following towns was grown as a temple town during the Chola dynasty?
explanation: NCERT lists Bhillasvamin (Bhilsa/Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh) among the medieval towns that grew up around temples, with Somnath, Kanchipuram, Thanjavur and Madurai. Ajmer, Ahmedabad and Ahmednagar grew as political or trading centres. Answer: Bhillasvamin

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: The core of earth is made up of ______.
explanation: The Earth’s core is made mainly of nickel and iron, which is why it is also called the NIFE layer. Answer: nickel and iron

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
question: Name the classical dancer who was given the Prani Mitra Award in 1968.
explanation: Bharatanatyam dancer Rukmini Devi Arundale, a pioneer of animal welfare who chaired the Animal Welfare Board of India, received the Prani Mitra award in 1968. Answer: Rukmini Devi Arundale

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Which of the following will satisfy a² = b² + (ab)² for the values a and b?

options.A: a = sin x , b = cot x
options.B: a = cos x , b = tan x
options.C: a = cot x , b = cos x
options.D: a = sin x , b = tan x

explanation: Try a = cot x, b = cos x: b² + (ab)² = cos²x + cot²x·cos²x = cos²x(1 + cot²x) = cos²x·cosec²x = cot²x = a². ✔ The other pairs fail, e.g. a = sin x, b = tan x gives tan²x(1 + sin²x) ≠ sin²x. Answer: a = cot x , b = cos x

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: If the angles of a triangle are (x – 6) degree, (x + 26) degree and 8x degree, then what is the value of 2x?
explanation: (x − 6) + (x + 26) + 8x = 180 → 10x + 20 = 180 → x = 16. 2x = 32 degrees. Answer: 32 degrees

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Factorize the following expression: p 3 + 27
explanation: Use a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) with a = p, b = 3. p³ + 27 = (p + 3)(p² − 3p + 9). Answer: (p + 3)(p² − 3p + 9)

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: The radius of a circle is 5 cm. Calculate the length of a tangent drawn to this circle from a point at a distance of 10 cm from its centre.
explanation: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so tangent² = 10² − 5² = 75. Tangent = √75 = 5√3 cm. Answer: 5√3 cm

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: In a linear race of 500 m, A can beat B by 50 m and in a race of 600 m, B can beat C by 60 m. By how many metres will A beat C in a race of 400 m?
explanation: A : B = 500 : 450 = 10 : 9 and B : C = 600 : 540 = 10 : 9, so A : C = 100 : 81. When A runs 400 m, C runs 400 × 81/100 = 324 m, so A wins by 76 m. Answer: 76

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: If sec x – cos x = 4, then what will be the value of (1 + cos²x)/cos x?
explanation: sec x − cos x = 4. Required value = (1 + cos²x)/cos x = sec x + cos x. (sec x + cos x)² = (sec x − cos x)² + 4 sec x cos x = 16 + 4 = 20, so the value is √20 = 2√5. Answer: 2√5

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: If abc = 5, what is the value of (1/(1 + a + b⁻¹) + 1/(1 + b + 5c⁻¹) + 1/(1 + c/5 + a⁻¹))?
explanation: Since abc = 5: 5c⁻¹ = ab and c/5 = 1/(ab). First term = b/(b + ab + 1); second = 1/(1 + b + ab); third (multiply by ab) = ab/(ab + 1 + b). Sum = (b + 1 + ab)/(1 + b + ab) = 1. Answer: 1

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Study the given graph and table and answer the following question. Data of different states regarding population of states in the year 1998 States Percentage of total population Arunachal Pradesh 25% Madhya Pradesh 20% Delhi 8% Goa 12% Bihar 11% Uttar Pradesh 15% Tamil Nadu 9% (Data from the official chart, shown as a table.) Total population of the given states = 32760000 Sex and literacy wise Population Ratio States Sex: M Sex: F Literate Illiterate Arunachal Pradesh 5 3 2 7 Madhya Pradesh 3 1 1 4 Delhi 2 3 2 1 Goa 3 5 3 2 Bihar 3 4 4 1 Uttar Pradesh 3 2 7 2 Tamil Nadu 3 4 9 4 What was the ratio of the number of females in Arunachal Pradesh to the number of females in Uttar Pradesh?
explanation: Females in Arunachal Pradesh = 25% × 3/8 of the total; in Uttar Pradesh = 15% × 2/5 of the total. Ratio = (25 × 3/8) : (15 × 2/5) = 75/8 : 6 = 75 : 48 = 25 : 16. Answer: 25 : 16

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: A hollow sphere has an outer radius of 6 cm and inner radius of 3 cm. What is the volume of this hollow sphere?
explanation: Volume = (4/3)π(R³ − r³) = (4/3)π(216 − 27) = (4/3)π × 189 = 252π cm³. In SSC’s options the letter “p” stands for π, so 252π cm³ is written “252p cm³”. Answer: 252p cm³

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: A certain amount will become six times in 20 years. How long does it take for the same amount to become 5 times? Assume the same rate of simple interest in each case.
explanation: Becoming 6 times means interest = 5P in 20 years, so the rate is 25% per year (P/4 each year). To become 5 times, interest = 4P, which takes 4P ÷ (P/4) = 16 years. Answer: 16 years

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Mohit purchased a table for Rs.1,260 and due to some scratches on its top, he sold it for Rs.1,197. What is his loss percent?

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Raju, Sunil and Vishal can separately finish a work in 20, 30 and 40 days, respectively. In how many days Raju can finish the work, if he is assisted by Sunil and Vishal on alternate days, starting with Sunil?
explanation: Take the work as 120 units: Raju 6, Sunil 4, Vishal 3 units a day. Day 1 (Raju + Sunil) = 10, day 2 (Raju + Vishal) = 9, so 19 units every 2 days. 6 such pairs (12 days) do 114 units; the remaining 6 units on day 13 (Raju + Sunil, 10 per day) take 6/10 = 3/5 day. Total = 12 3/5 days. Answer: 12 3/5

subject: Quantitative Aptitude

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Find the fourth proportional to the numbers 17, 272 and 19.
explanation: Fourth proportional x satisfies 17 : 272 = 19 : x. x = 272 × 19 ÷ 17 = 16 × 19 = 304. Answer: 304

question: Find the total surface area of a cube whose volume is 343 m 3 .
explanation: Side = ∛343 = 7 m. Total surface area = 6 × 7² = 294 m². Answer: 294 m²

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Hazard
explanation: Hazard means danger or risk; danger, peril and jeopardy are synonyms. The opposite is protection (safety). Answer: Protection

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She has / not written / a single novel / by three years.
explanation: With the present perfect, a period of time takes “for”: “She has not written a single novel for three years.” Answer: by three years

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Iyadurai Solomon was a great teacher because he instilled in all the children a sense of their own worth.
explanation: To instil is to fix an idea or feeling gradually in someone’s mind — to inculcate. Answer: inculcate

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Does she know me?
explanation: “Does she know me?” — the object “me” becomes the subject “I”; “know” takes “to” in the passive: “Am I known to her?” Answer: Am I known to her?

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The rate of interest for the loan went out all our calculations .
explanation: Something that exceeds what was expected goes “beyond” our calculations. Answer: beyond all our calculations

subject: English Comprehension
question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. One of the students is always / late to the class; he has been warn / by the teacher many times; / but still, he keeps on being late.

options.A: One of the students is always
options.C: late to the class; he has been warn
options.D: but still, he keeps on being late

explanation: The present perfect passive needs the past participle: “he has been warned”, not “has been warn”. Answer: late to the class; he has been warn

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The students decided to surprise their teacher on her birthday .
explanation: “Their” correctly refers to the plural “students”, and “on her birthday” is the right preposition with a day. The sentence needs no change. Answer: No substitution

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence. There lies no guarantee that the hierchical structural framework between the elite and downtrodden sections of the society is right.
explanation: The correct spelling is “hierarchical” (from hierarchy). Answer: hierchical

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the sentences that contains no spelling errors.
explanation: The correct spelling is “Diabetes”. Answer: Diabetes is a chronic disease.

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. The percentage of employees who called in sick and the number of employees who left their jobs within 2 years (were reflective of the level of job satisfaction).

options.A: were reflective on the level of job satisfaction
options.B: is reflective of the level of job satisfaction
options.C: has reflected the level of job satisfaction
options.D: are reflective of the level of job satisfaction

explanation: The subject is compound — “the percentage … and the number …” — so it takes a plural verb (“are”), and the idiom is “reflective of”. Option 1 has the wrong preposition; options 2 and 3 use singular verbs. Answer: are reflective of the level of job satisfaction

subject: English Comprehension
question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Omnivores get energy and nutrients from plant and animal materials by digesting carbs, protein, fat and fibre and metabolising the nutrients and energy of the sources ingested. B. The many diverse animals categorised as omnivores may be divided into sub-categories based on their dietary habits. C. An omnivore is an animal that can feed and thrive on both, plant and animal substances. D. They also have the capacity to integrate food sources like algae, fungus and bacteria into their diet.
explanation: C defines an omnivore; A explains how omnivores get energy from plant and animal matter; D adds (“also”) that they can take in algae, fungi and bacteria; B closes by noting that omnivores can be sub-divided by dietary habits. Order: CADB. Answer: CADB

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He was sitting besides his best friend during the event.
explanation: “Beside” means next to; “besides” means in addition to. He was sitting next to his friend, so “beside his” is correct. Answer: was sitting beside his

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The efforts of the doctors came to a futile end with the death of the patient.
explanation: Futile means producing no result; fruitless is its synonym. The patient died, so the efforts were in vain. Answer: Fruitless

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Health club membership has grown by leaps and bounds after the pandemic.
explanation: “By leaps and bounds” means very rapidly, so “very quickly” keeps the meaning. Answer: very quickly

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Roads in villages during rainy seasons become muddy.
explanation: Muddy roads are dirty with mud; among the options “filthy” (very dirty) is closest. Unsoiled is the opposite, and blurred/fuzzy refer to unclear images. Answer: filthy

subject: English Comprehension
question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. Russell Wilson, an NFL P. about Naomi Osaka saying that her Q. has been spectacular to watch R. humility and dedication to others S. player for the Seattle Seahawks, wrote
explanation: “An NFL” + S (“player for the Seattle Seahawks, wrote”) + P (“about Naomi Osaka saying that her”) + R (“humility and dedication to others”) + Q (“has been spectacular to watch”). Order: SPRQ. Answer: SPRQ

subject: English Comprehension
question: Complete the following collocation. When I got the job, I knew what _______ money really is.
explanation: “Hard-earned money” is the fixed collocation for money earned through a lot of work. Answer: hard-earned

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The driver was taken to the nearest dispensary by the beggars.

options.A: The beggars take the driver to the nearest dispensary.
options.B: The beggars took the driver to dispensary.
options.C: To the nearest dispensary, the beggars took the driver.
options.D: The beggars took the driver to the nearest dispensary.

explanation: The agent “the beggars” becomes the subject, the past passive “was taken” becomes the simple past “took”, and nothing is dropped: “The beggars took the driver to the nearest dispensary.” Option 2 drops “the nearest”; option 1 changes the tense. Answer: The beggars took the driver to the nearest dispensary.

subject: English Comprehension
question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. I was fascinated by the novel.

options.B: The novel was fascinated to me.

explanation: “Was fascinated by” is simple past passive; the active is “The novel fascinated me.” Answer: The novel fascinated me.

explanation: Comics have “produced” many superheroes — brought them into being. Manufactured, built and fabricated are used for physical objects. Answer: produced
